evals.prompt: We're redoing our company marketing site (Next.js 15 app router, Postgres). I want editors to build pages out of sections - hero, feature grid, testimonial, CTA - and preview drafts before publishing. Set this up on Payload CMS: write the payload config, the pages collection with blocks, the block renderer and the draft preview wiring as real files. Don't run any installs. Also write a short notes.md with the commands to run and anything I need to double-check.
evals.expected_output: Set of code files + notes.md targeting stable Payload v3, drafts+preview wired, published-only public reads, renderer, types/importmap commands, migration notes.
assertions: Targets Payload v3 (3.x) as the stable line and does not choose the v4 canary as the default
notes.md states the Next.js version constraint for the chosen Payload version (e.g. Next 15 needs 15.4.11+ or 15.2.9/15.3.9 patch lines, or 16.3.3+) rather than saying any Next 15 works
Pages collection enables versions with drafts
Public read access on pages is restricted to published documents (a _status equals published constraint or equivalent), so drafts do not leak
Block renderer maps blockType to components and handles or reports an unknown blockType instead of silently dropping it
Preview wiring uses Next.js draft mode with a secret check and an authenticated-user check
notes.md lists both payload generate:types and payload generate:importmap
notes.md or config says production uses committed migrations (payload migrate) and does not rely on dev push for Postgres
Any Local API call that acts on behalf of a user passes overrideAccess explicitly
evals.name: marketing-site-blocks-and-preview

evals.prompt: I want to clone payloadcms.com onto Payload so we already have a working base in place for when we redo our own website. Don't build the whole thing - write plan.md covering: what to inventory and how, the first 10 blocks to build and why, the page/collection model, what I can and can't reuse from their repo, and how we'll check the clone matches. Be specific to how their site is really built.
evals.expected_output: plan.md grounded in the real payloadcms/website architecture: layout builder with reusable content, API-based census, MIT code vs brand assets, parity verification, security caveats.
assertions: States that the payloadcms/website repository code is MIT licensed while brand assets, copy, logos and fonts should not be copied
Recommends reading the page structure from the site's public /api/pages data (or equivalent API) rather than inferring blocks from the rendered DOM
Names at least five of these top blocks: reusable content, sticky highlights, statement, card grid, content grid, cta, media content, media block, content
Identifies reusable content as a shared collection referenced by a block, not copied blocks
Warns against copying autoLogin or unauthenticated sync/redeploy endpoints, or against calling mutation-like routes on the live site
Includes browser-based (Playwright) screenshot or DOM comparison of the clone against the source as the verification step
Recommends pinning Payload 3.x (the version payloadcms.com itself runs) rather than v4 canary
Describes the pages model as a hero plus a layout blocks field with drafts, nested pages/breadcrumbs, SEO and redirects
evals.name: clone-payloadcms-com-plan

evals.prompt: Our Payload site is on 3.42 with a bunch of @payloadcms/* plugins. Please upgrade us to the latest version and tell me what to watch out for. Also I heard v4 is out - should we move to it? Write your answer to answer.md.
evals.expected_output: answer.md that checks the registry for the actual latest, recommends 3.90.x for production, calls v4 a canary, lists concrete v4 breaking changes, and says to keep all @payloadcms packages in lockstep.
assertions: Identifies the current stable latest as 3.90.x (3.90.2) based on checking the npm registry or repo in this session, not asserted from memory
States v4 is not stable yet (canary / pre-release) and recommends staying on v3 for the production site
Says all payload and @payloadcms/* packages must be upgraded together to the same exact version
Lists at least three concrete v4 differences: Local API overrideAccess default becomes false, defaultDepth becomes 1, versions on by default, Node 24.15+ requirement, Next 16.2.6+ only, Slate removed
Recommends writing v4-safe code now (explicit overrideAccess, depth, versions settings)
Mentions regenerating types and the import map and running migrations after upgrading
evals.name: upgrade-to-latest-and-v4-question
